newsitem.title: UK: Horlick held detailed talks with ABN - paper.
newsitem.headline: Horlick held detailed talks with ABN - paper.

text.p: The Observer newspaper alleged in a report that former Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) fund manager Nicola Horlick held detailed talks with ABN AMRO about joining the Dutch bank to set up a new investment unit.

The report alleged that Nick Bannister, chief executive of ABN AMRO's securities unit Hoare Govett, presented a business plan to Horlick earlier this month and that ABN earmarked a possible office location for the new unit.

Horlick was suspended by Morgan Grenfell on January 14 just days after being promoted managing director of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) amid allegations she planned to defect to ABN AMRO and was soliciting MGAM colleagues to go with her.
Last week Horlick, who has conducted a high-profile campaign since her suspension, admitted she had been in talks with another firm but said those contacts had ended before her suspension.

Asked to comment on the Observer allegations, a spokesman for Horlick told Reuters: "She has consistently denied any attempt to poach staff...talks with ABN were informal and preliminary and had been terminated."
The Observer also said Keith Percy, ousted from DMG's MGAM last year, had been pencilled in as chief investment officer of the new ABN AMRO business.

A DMG spokesman told Reuters: "The position remains unchanged, Horlick is no longer an employee and there are no plans either to compensate or reinstate her. The matter is closed as far as we are concerned."

ABN AMRO continued to fend off queries about its alleged involvement. Company spokesman Tanno Massar told Reuters: "We've said all we want to say and we will not have this standpoint influenced by new developments...really there is nothing we want to add."
